Recap (short):

- Primary goals: predictable p50/p95 latency for interactive flows, cost predictability for batched async jobs, and SOC2/aligned auditability.

Immediate asks (what we need from you):

3) Availability/SLA needs: required uptime and acceptable failover behavior (auto-fallback to smaller models, region fallback).
4) Security constraints: Does procurement require Private/VPC or is a Dedicated deployment in our isolated tenancy sufficient? Any required KMS/HSM integrations or on-prem audit collectors?

Preliminary Dedicated sizing questions (we'll validate once we receive traffic):
- Preferred GPUs: do you have infra constraints (NVIDIA A10/A100/H100) in your procurement list? If not, we can propose a GPU mix.
- Concurrency model: do you prefer lower-latency single-request concurrency or higher throughput with batching? Typical trade-offs below.

Adding some initial sizing heuristics so Ethan's team can sanity-check before the workbook:

Assumptions (example workload):
- Token mix: 55% short (<64 tokens), 30% mid (64–512), 15% long (>512, up to 1,200)
- Peak TPS target: 2,000 requests/sec (requests are not uniformly token-length distributed)
- Latency preference: interactive short requests p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms

Rough Dedicated guidance (very coarse, will refine with actual histograms):
- Option A (latency-first): H100 (or grouped H100-equivalent) with 1:8 concurrency tuning. Expected short-prompt p50 ~90–130ms; good p95 on <256 token requests. Cost: high.
- Option B (cost-balanced): Mix of A100-80GB for mids/longs + A10/NVIDIA L4 for short prompts with smart routing. Use caching for repeated prefixes. Better $/token but slightly higher p95 for tail L >512 tokens.
- Option C (throughput-batched): A100 with aggressive batching (higher queueing SLO) — good for async jobs but p50 increases for interactive flows.

Key notes:
- Token mix is the biggest driver. If long token requests are only 5–7%, you can optimize with a smaller fleet targeted at long jobs and keep the interactive pool lean.
- Quantization (int8) can change throughput economics significantly; we can produce profile curves once we have model choices.

I'll prep a short tab in the workbook with these options and example cost/latency rows.

-Karthik
